findings.problem: `PaginationParams` gained an `After` field and a `ToGraphQLParams` method that only forwards to `CursorPaginationParams.ToGraphQLParams` and silently drops `Page`. Nothing outside tests calls it, since both GraphQL tools use `OptionalCursorPaginationParams`. As a result, `OptionalPaginationParams` now reads an `after` argument for every REST tool even though none of them declares it. This leaves two overlapping pagination types.
findings.fix: Remove `After` and `ToGraphQLParams` from `PaginationParams`, and stop reading `after` in `OptionalPaginationParams`. Leave cursor handling only in `CursorPaginationParams` in `pagination.go`. Delete `TestPaginationParams_ToGraphQLParams` (`server_test.go:585`) and the `after` cases in `TestOptionalPaginationParams`. If a tool later needs page-to-cursor conversion, add it to `pagination.go` along with its caller.

findings.problem: `WithUnifiedPagination` is new exported API with no caller in the package. It promises page-to-cursor conversion that nothing implements, because no parser reads `page` and turns it into a cursor.
findings.fix: Delete `WithUnifiedPagination` and `TestWithUnifiedPagination`. Add it back together with the first tool and parser that use it.

findings.problem: The `perPage` schema now exists in two places: `withPaginationPerPage` in `pagination.go` and the inline copy in `WithPagination` (`server.go:181`). The default of 30 is also repeated as `DefaultGraphQLPageSize` and as a literal in `OptionalPaginationParams` (`server.go:224`). Pagination code is split between `server.go` and `pagination.go`.
findings.fix: Move `WithPagination`, `PaginationParams` and `OptionalPaginationParams` from `server.go` into `pagination.go`. Make `WithPagination` use `withPaginationPerPage()`. Add one `DefaultPageSize = 30` constant and use it for both the REST and GraphQL defaults. Also remove the empty `//` comment line above `DefaultGraphQLPageSize` (line 11).

findings.problem: The new `list_sub_issues` tool declares its own `page` and `per_page` parameters, with no min or max limits, and parses them by hand. Every other list tool uses `WithPagination()` / `OptionalPaginationParams` with `perPage`, so this tool has a different parameter name and no validation.
findings.fix: Replace the two `mcp.WithNumber` options with `WithPagination()`. Replace the hand-written `page`/`per_page` parsing with `pagination, err := OptionalPaginationParams(request)` and use `pagination.Page` and `pagination.PerPage`. Update `sub_issue_test.go` to send `perPage`, and update the toolsnap.

findings.problem: `DescriptionRepositoryOwner` and `DescriptionRepositoryName` are package-wide constants but are declared in `actions.go`. Newly written files, such as `sub_issue.go:26` and `discussions.go`, still use the literal strings "Repository owner" and "Repository name", so the constants are only partly used.
findings.fix: Move the constants to a shared file such as `server.go` or `tools.go`. Use them in the new and changed tools (`sub_issue.go`, `discussions.go`), or add `WithOwnerRepo()`-style ToolOptions for the required `owner`/`repo` pair.

findings.problem: The four `switch` cases in `ListDiscussions` repeat the same block: declare the query struct, call `client.Query`, map the error, and copy `query.Repository.Discussions`. Only the struct tag differs between them. Each new filter will double the number of cases.
findings.fix: Declare four named query types at package level. Give each a `connection() discussionsConnection` method, matching a small interface. Have the switch only choose which type to use, then make one `client.Query(ctx, q, vars)` call with one error check and one `conn = q.connection()`.

findings.problem: `Test_ListDiscussions` chooses the mocked query and variables with `switch tc.name` on the test-case name string. If a case is renamed or added without updating the switch, `httpClient` stays nil and the test hits the real client or fails in a confusing way. It also separates each case's inputs from its expectations.
findings.fix: Add a `matcher githubv4mock.Matcher` field (or `query`, `vars` and `response` fields) to the test-case struct. Set it in each case and build `httpClient` from `tc.matcher`, using no matcher for the perPage-rejection case. Then remove the switch.
